A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SamS research. All 26 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original alignment experiments, HH/SHP evaluations, noise tests, ablations, computational measurements, and GPT-based dataset analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, reward construction, exploitation/exploration networks, encoder, pretraining, and historical sample pool are unchanged. Integration with Selective DPO was already documented in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same UltraFeedback-derived datasets, Anthropic-HH, SHP, AlpacaEval 2, and MT-Bench, including the same noise scenarios. The revised HH sample count concerns experimental settings rather than coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the matched experiments. Selective DPO and Selective DPO+SamS move from v1 Appendix D.4 to v2 Section 5.5; neither is newly evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported HH training-set size changes from 16,800 in v1 Table 4 to 160,800 in v2 Table 5, a nearly tenfold revision to the stated data budget. Other settings are retained. The PDFs do not explain whether this corrects documentation or reflects different training, and do not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: The selection-ratio and exploration-network ablations, label-noise tests, computational analysis, and GPT-judged examples are retained. Appendix D.5 becomes D.4 without changing its analyses.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed, uncertainty, and significance reporting do not change. The same point estimates and learning curves are presented.

E6.justification: Reported benchmark scores, ablation accuracies, learning curves, runtime measurements, and GPT-judgment outcomes are unchanged. The relocated Selective DPO comparison, v1 Table 6 versus v2 Table 3, has identical result entries.

T1.justification: The contextual-bandit formulation, reward definitions, optimization equations, and Appendix F mathematics are retained. No theorem, proof, assumption, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive sample scheduling, improved alignment, robustness, and limited computational overhead.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning sample quality, difficult responses, noise robustness, and efficiency remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the limitation that benefits diminish with higher-quality preference data; the pre-selection discussion is relocated.

D1.justification: Encoder initialization and pretraining, scheduler hyperparameters, sample-pool implementation, response-generation instructions, eight-A100 hardware disclosure, runtime information, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds six references, including Transformer Copilot, LLM-Forest, and bandit/active-learning papers, and removes Qin et al.'s contextual combinatorial bandit reference. These localized citation changes do not substantially revise the research positioning.

P1.justification: The pre-selection comparison moves from Appendix D.4 to Section 5.5, with corresponding cross-reference updates. v2 adds acknowledgments and revises author/conference header text; most prose remains verbatim.

P2.justification: The pre-selection table moves into the main text as Table 3, other tables are renumbered, and the compact author block changes pagination and spacing. Figures 1–5 retain identical graphic content.

improvement.justification: Moving the existing Selective DPO comparison and runtime tradeoff into Section 5.5 makes evaluation against the closest alternative easier to assess. This is a limited presentation benefit: methods and results are unchanged, and the unexplained HH count revision cannot be credited as improved experimental evidence.
